messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Let's add a new feature—bots. Bots can be members of rooms and post messages via an HTTP API.

Any chat member can create and manage bots via the user interface:
- open the account settings page (`/account/edit`)
- click the bot icon ("Set up chat bots")

This opens the bots page (`/bots`). It lists the bots you created (administrators see all bots) and has the "Add a chat bot" button. The button opens the `/bots/new` page with a form:

- bot avatar (optional)
- bot name (required), labelled "Name the bot"
- the "Save changes" button

Submitting the form creates a bot and redirects back to `/bots`. Each bot on the list shows its name and its unique bot code in a read-only field labelled "Bot code", in the same list item—the code is used to authenticate bot requests. The bot code is a sensitive credential. The bots page shows all of your bots on one page, without pagination.

From the list, you can also edit a bot (name, avatar): each bot has an "Edit <bot name>" link (for example, "Edit Deploy Bot") to its edit page. The edit page uses the same form and has a "Delete this chat bot" button that asks for confirmation. A deleted bot can no longer post messages.

Like any new user, a new bot joins all open rooms. Bots can be added to other rooms the same way as people.

Here is how a bot can post a message:

```
curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \
  https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages
```

Bots can post from shell scripts and CI jobs. The raw request body becomes the message body. No JSON envelope, no field names.

The endpoint responds with:

- `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`
- `422 Unprocessable Content` — empty body and no attachment
- `404 Not Found` — bad room id
- `401 Unauthorized` — invalid bot code

The message is broadcast to connected clients and triggers push notifications exactly as a human-authored message would.

The message shows the bot (its name) as the author.

5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust

Rails.application.routes.draw do
  root "welcome#show"

  resource :first_run

  resource :session do
    scope module: "sessions" do
      resources :transfers, only: %i[ show update ]
    end
  end

  resource :account do
    scope module: "accounts" do
      resources :users

      resource :join_code, only: :create
      resource :logo, only: %i[ show destroy ]
      resource :custom_styles, only: %i[ edit update ]
    end
  end

  direct :fresh_account_logo do |options|
    route_for :account_logo, v: Current.account&.updated_at&.to_fs(:number), size: options[:size]
  end

  get "join/:join_code", to: "users#new", as: :join
  post "join/:join_code", to: "users#create"

  resources :qr_code, only: :show

  resources :users, only: :show do
    scope module: "users" do
      resource :avatar, only: %i[ show destroy ]
      resource :ban, only: %i[ create destroy ]

      scope defaults: { user_id: "me" } do
        resource :sidebar, only: :show
        resource :profile
        resources :push_subscriptions do
          scope module: "push_subscriptions" do
            resources :test_notifications, only: :create
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  namespace :autocompletable do
    resources :users, only: :index
  end

  direct :fresh_user_avatar do |user, options|
    route_for :user_avatar, user.avatar_token, v: user.updated_at.to_fs(:number)
  end

  resources :rooms do
    resources :messages

    scope module: "rooms" do
      resource :refresh, only: :show
      resource :settings, only: :show
      resource :involvement, only: %i[ show update ]
    end

    get "@:message_id", to: "rooms#show", as: :at_message
  end

  namespace :rooms do
    resources :opens
    resources :closeds
    resources :directs
  end

  resources :messages do
    scope module: "messages" do
      resources :boosts
    end
  end

  resources :searches, only: %i[ index create ] do
    delete :clear, on: :collection
  end

  resource :unfurl_link, only: :create

  get "webmanifest"    => "pwa#manifest"
  get "service-worker" => "pwa#service_worker"

  get "up" => "rails/health#show", as: :rails_health_check
end

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first

class ApplicationSystemTestCase < ActionDispatch::SystemTestCase
  driven_by :selenium, using: :headless_chrome, screen_size: [ 1400, 1400 ]

require "application_system_test_case"

class SendingMessagesTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  setup do
    sign_in "jz@37signals.com"
    join_room rooms(:designers)
  end

  test "sending messages between two users" do
    using_session("Kevin") do
      sign_in "kevin@37signals.com"
      join_room rooms(:designers)
    end

    join_room rooms(:designers)
    send_message "Is this thing on?"

    using_session("Kevin") do
      join_room rooms(:designers)
      assert_message_text "Is this thing on?"

      send_message "👍👍"
    end

    join_room rooms(:designers)
    assert_message_text "👍👍"
  end

  test "editing messages" do
    using_session("Kevin") do
      sign_in "kevin@37signals.com"
      join_room rooms(:designers)
    end

    within_message messages(:third) do
      reveal_message_actions
      find(".message__edit-btn").click
      fill_in_rich_text_area "message_body", with: "Redacted!"
      click_on "Save changes"
    end

    using_session("Kevin") do
      join_room rooms(:designers)

      assert_message_text "Redacted!"
    end
  end

  test "deleting messages" do
    using_session("Kevin") do
      sign_in "kevin@37signals.com"
      join_room rooms(:designers)

      assert_message_text "Third time's a charm."
    end

    within_message messages(:third) do
      reveal_message_actions
      find(".message__edit-btn").click

      accept_confirm do
        click_on "Delete message"
      end
    end

    using_session("Kevin") do
      assert_message_text "Third time's a charm.", count: 0
    end
  end
end

class FirstRun
  ACCOUNT_NAME = "Campfire"
  FIRST_ROOM_NAME = "All Talk"

  def self.create!(user_params)
    account = Account.create!(name: ACCOUNT_NAME)
    room    = Rooms::Open.new(name: FIRST_ROOM_NAME)

    administrator = room.creator = User.new(user_params.merge(role: :administrator))
    room.save!

    room.memberships.grant_to administrator

    administrator
  end
end
module MessagesHelper
  def message_area_tag(room, &)
    tag.div id: "message-area", class: "message-area", contents: true, data: {
      controller: "messages presence drop-target",
      action: [ messages_actions, drop_target_actions, presence_actions ].join(" "),
      messages_first_of_day_class: "message--first-of-day",
      messages_formatted_class: "message--formatted",
      messages_me_class: "message--me",
      messages_mentioned_class: "message--mentioned",
      messages_threaded_class: "message--threaded",
      messages_page_url_value: room_messages_url(room)
    }, &
  end

  def messages_tag(room, &)
    tag.div id: dom_id(room, :messages), class: "messages", data: {
      controller: "maintain-scroll refresh-room",
      action: [ maintain_scroll_actions, refresh_room_actions ].join(" "),
      messages_target: "messages",
      refresh_room_loaded_at_value: room.updated_at.to_fs(:epoch),
      refresh_room_url_value: room_refresh_url(room)
    }, &
  end

  def message_tag(message, &)
    message_timestamp_milliseconds = message.created_at.to_fs(:epoch)

    tag.div id: dom_id(message),
      class: "message #{"message--emoji" if message.plain_text_body.all_emoji?}",
      data: {
        controller: "reply",
        user_id: message.creator_id,
        message_id: message.id,
        message_timestamp: message_timestamp_milliseconds,
        message_updated_at: message.updated_at.to_fs(:epoch),
        sort_value: message_timestamp_milliseconds,
        messages_target: "message",
        search_results_target: "message",
        refresh_room_target: "message",
        reply_composer_outlet: "#composer"
      }, &
  rescue Exception => e
    Sentry.capture_exception(e, extra: { message: message })
    Rails.logger.error "Exception while rendering message #{message.class.name}##{message.id}, failed with: #{e.class} `#{e.message}`"

    render "messages/unrenderable"
  end

  def message_timestamp(message, **attributes)
    local_datetime_tag message.created_at, **attributes
  end

  def message_presentation(message)
    case message.content_type
    when "attachment"
      message_attachment_presentation(message)
    when "sound"
      message_sound_presentation(message)
    else
      auto_link h(ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters.apply(message.body.body)), html: { target: "_blank" }
    end
  rescue Exception => e
    Sentry.capture_exception(e, extra: { message: message })
    Rails.logger.error "Exception while generating message representation for #{message.class.name}##{message.id}, failed with: #{e.class} `#{e.message}`"

    ""
  end

  private
    def messages_actions
      "turbo:before-stream-render@document->messages#beforeStreamRender keydown.up@document->messages#editMyLastMessage"
    end

    def maintain_scroll_actions
      "turbo:before-stream-render@document->maintain-scroll#beforeStreamRender"
    end

    def refresh_room_actions
      "visibilitychange@document->refresh-room#visibilityChanged online@window->refresh-room#online"
    end

    def presence_actions
      "visibilitychange@document->presence#visibilityChanged"
    end

    def message_attachment_presentation(message)
      Messages::AttachmentPresentation.new(message, context: self).render
    end

    def message_sound_presentation(message)
      sound = message.sound

      tag.div class: "sound", data: { controller: "sound", action: "messages:play->sound#play", sound_url_value: asset_path(sound.asset_path) } do
        play_button + (sound.image ? sound_image_tag(sound.image) : sound.text)
      end
    end

    def play_button
      tag.button "🔊", class: "btn btn--plain", data: { action: "sound#play" }
    end

    def sound_image_tag(image)
      image_tag image.asset_path, width: image.width, height: image.height, class: "align--middle"
    end

    def message_author_title(author)
      [ author.name, author.bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
    end
end

module MessagesHelper
  def message_area_tag(room, &)
    tag.div id: "message-area", class: "message-area", contents: true, data: {
      controller: "messages presence drop-target",
      action: [ messages_actions, drop_target_actions, presence_actions ].join(" "),
      messages_first_of_day_class: "message--first-of-day",
      messages_formatted_class: "message--formatted",
      messages_me_class: "message--me",
      messages_mentioned_class: "message--mentioned",
      messages_threaded_class: "message--threaded",
      messages_page_url_value: room_messages_url(room)
    }, &
  end

  def messages_tag(room, &)
    tag.div id: dom_id(room, :messages), class: "messages", data: {
      controller: "maintain-scroll refresh-room",
      action: [ maintain_scroll_actions, refresh_room_actions ].join(" "),
      messages_target: "messages",
      refresh_room_loaded_at_value: room.updated_at.to_fs(:epoch),
      refresh_room_url_value: room_refresh_url(room)
    }, &
  end

  def message_tag(message, &)
    message_timestamp_milliseconds = message.created_at.to_fs(:epoch)

    tag.div id: dom_id(message),
      class: "message #{"message--emoji" if message.plain_text_body.all_emoji?}",
      data: {
        controller: "reply",
        user_id: message.creator_id,
        message_id: message.id,
        message_timestamp: message_timestamp_milliseconds,
        message_updated_at: message.updated_at.to_fs(:epoch),
        sort_value: message_timestamp_milliseconds,
        messages_target: "message",
        search_results_target: "message",
        refresh_room_target: "message",
        reply_composer_outlet: "#composer"
      }, &
  rescue Exception => e
    Sentry.capture_exception(e, extra: { message: message })
    Rails.logger.error "Exception while rendering message #{message.class.name}##{message.id}, failed with: #{e.class} `#{e.message}`"

    render "messages/unrenderable"
  end

  def message_timestamp(message, **attributes)
    local_datetime_tag message.created_at, **attributes
  end

  def message_presentation(message)
    case message.content_type
    when "attachment"
      message_attachment_presentation(message)
    when "sound"
      message_sound_presentation(message)
    else
      auto_link h(ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters.apply(message.body.body)), html: { target: "_blank" }
    end
  rescue Exception => e
    Sentry.capture_exception(e, extra: { message: message })
    Rails.logger.error "Exception while generating message representation for #{message.class.name}##{message.id}, failed with: #{e.class} `#{e.message}`"

    ""
  end

  private
    def messages_actions
      "turbo:before-stream-render@document->messages#beforeStreamRender keydown.up@document->messages#editMyLastMessage"
    end

    def maintain_scroll_actions
      "turbo:before-stream-render@document->maintain-scroll#beforeStreamRender"
    end

    def refresh_room_actions
      "visibilitychange@document->refresh-room#visibilityChanged online@window->refresh-room#online"
    end

    def presence_actions
      "visibilitychange@document->presence#visibilityChanged"
    end

    def message_attachment_presentation(message)
      Messages::AttachmentPresentation.new(message, context: self).render
    end

    def message_sound_presentation(message)
      sound = message.sound

      tag.div class: "sound", data: { controller: "sound", action: "messages:play->sound#play", sound_url_value: asset_path(sound.asset_path) } do
        play_button + (sound.image ? sound_image_tag(sound.image) : sound.text)
      end
    end

    def play_button
      tag.button "🔊", class: "btn btn--plain", data: { action: "sound#play" }
    end

    def sound_image_tag(image)
      image_tag image.asset_path, width: image.width, height: image.height, class: "align--middle"
    end

    def message_author_title(author)
      [ author.name, author.bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
    end
end

*   Any chat member can create and manage bots through the UI. This is the user-facing part, so it's critical.
    *   Account settings (`/account/edit`) will include a "Set up chat bots" link (with the bot icon) that opens the bots page (`/bots`).
    *   The `/bots` page will list created bots, with an "Add a chat bot" button.
    *   The "Add a chat bot" button will open the `/bots/new` page which has the form with:
        *   bot avatar (optional)
        *   bot name (required) labelled "Name the bot"
        *   the "Save changes" button.
    *   Submitting the form will create the bot and redirect back to `/bots`.
    *   The `/bots` page will display the bot name and a read-only "Bot code" field. The bot code is very sensitive!
    *   There's no pagination on the `/bots` page, meaning it shows all bots on one page.
    *   Each bot on the list is editable via an "Edit <bot name>" link, to its edit page.
    *   The edit page has the same form as the new bot page and includes a "Delete this chat bot" button, which requires confirmation. This is important: a deleted bot can no longer post messages.
*   Like new users, new bots will join all open rooms. They can be added to other rooms, just like people. That makes perfect sense.
*   The HTTP API for bot message posting:
    *   `curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages`

        *   `404 Not Found` for a bad room ID.
        *   `401 Unauthorized` for an invalid bot code.
    *   The message will be broadcast to connected clients and trigger push notifications just like any human message.
    *   The message will show the bot (its name) as the author.

3.  `SessionsController#create` also uses `User.not_bot.active.authenticate_by(...)`, so login forms are safe from bot logins.

Okay, let's break this down systematically. First, the route: `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages`. This needs to be implemented. I'm thinking of adding it under `resources :rooms` in `config/routes.rb`, maybe like `post ":bot_key/messages", to: "rooms/bot_messages#create", as: :bot_messages`. We have to make sure the `:bot_code` doesn't conflict with any existing routes in that scope; luckily, it doesn't.

Next, the response codes and the order of checks are crucial. The spec says `201 Created`, `422 Unprocessable Content`, `404 Not Found`, and `401 Unauthorized`. It's important to get the order right: does authentication happen before room lookup, or validation of the message body?  My guess is that authenticating the bot first (`before_action :authenticate_bot`) is the standard Rails way. If the room is bad, then it should return `404`, but if the bot code is invalid, then it should return `401`. But what if a valid bot posts to a room it's not a member of? "Bots can be members of rooms and post messages via an HTTP API". If a bot is not a member of a room, it should also be a `404` error (not found). This is consistent with our established patterns and keeps things clean.

The `Location` header is interesting. It specifies `/messages/:message_id`. This means we are going to use the `message_path(@message)` helper in our Rails controller. It's a relative path, and it will generate the correct relative URL to the message. That's a good approach to ensure consistency in our application's response.

module TrackedRoomVisit

  end

  end

  def last_room_visited
    Current.user.rooms.find_by(id: cookies[:last_room]) || default_room
  end

messages.thinking:
**Bot Code Security and Implementation**

Okay, let's break this down. First, regarding the exposure of the bot code: good news! We can leverage Rails' built-in parameter filtering. Looking at `config/initializers/filter_parameter_logging.rb`, we're already filtering `:token` and `:_key`.  If we consistently use names like `:bot_key` or `:bot_token` for route params, or add `:bot_code` to the filter list, those values will be automatically masked in our logs, which is great for security.  This also works because Rails will filter `bot_token` if the route param is `:bot_key` or `:bot_code` and we update the filter in `filter_parameter_logging.rb`. The only place we seem to expose it is the read-only input labelled "Bot code" on the `/bots` page to the bot's creator or an admin. No risk of exposure on the main user pages.

Now, let's re-examine the prompt and think carefully:  "The bot code is a sensitive credential."  This suggests we need to consider several things beyond just hiding the value.

1.  **Length and Randomness:**  We need cryptographically secure randomness, like that provided by `SecureRandom`.  A weak or predictable code would be disastrous.

2.  **Constant-Time Comparisons:** Crucially, we have to consider timing attacks. If we look up the `bot_code` in the database, like `User.active.bot.find_by(bot_token: bot_code)`, we must be careful.  If someone uses a known format like `"id-token"` and the bot token directly, there's a potential timing issue.

Let's look at the curl URL: `https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages`. If `bot_code` is `"#{id}-#{bot_token}"`, say, `42-xK9mPqR2vL8n`, or just the raw `bot_token` (e.g., `xK9mPqR2vL8n`), what are the implications?

*   If `bot_code` is `"#{id}-#{bot_token}"`:
    1.  It's guaranteed unique *without* a DB check! The ID is unique and it's paired with the bot_token.
    2.  We can look up the bot by the `id` first, and then *securely* compare the `bot_token` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare` (this is essential to avoid timing attacks).
*   If `bot_code` is just the `bot_token` (e.g., generated with `SecureRandom.base58(24)` and a unique index in the database), a `find_by(bot_token: ...)` is still fast and indexed. However, a constant time comparison is more difficult. This is mitigated because the caller just copies and pastes the value of "Bot code" into the URL.

The beauty of this is that it works in either case, regardless of how the caller expects the value. They don't need to know the internal structure.

What about URL-safe characters?  Should we avoid special characters in the `<bot-code>` part of the URL? `SecureRandom.base58(24)` or `SecureRandom.alphanumeric(24)` would be ideal as they only contain `[A-Za-z0-9]` and are 100% URL-safe. And if we want constant-time verification without leaking timing: we could hash/index the `bot_token`. However, the prompt indicates the code *must* be displayable on the `/bots` page. We need the actual, readable `bot_token` to render the bot code. `id-token` (like `4-kP9x...`) or `base58(24)` are great; `id-token` gives constant-time `secure_compare` on the secret part!

And if someone uses a regex or simply checks `bot.bot_token`? `SecureRandom.base58(24)` (the standard Rails `has_secure_token` format) or `"#{id}-#{bot_token}"` are ideal.

To fully understand and replicate this, let's inspect the `app/models/session.rb` and see how it generates the `token`.

module User::Bot

    has_many :created_bots, -> { bot }, class_name: "User", foreign_key: :creator_id, dependent: :nullify

  class_methods do

      return nil if bot_code.blank?

      active.bot.find_by(bot_token: bot_code)
    end
  end

  private
    def assign_bot_defaults
      self.password_digest ||= ""
      self.bot_token ||= generate_bot_token
    end

    def generate_bot_token
      loop do
        token = SecureRandom.base58(24)
        break token unless User.exists?(bot_token: token)
      end
    end
end

class Rooms::BotMessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :authenticate_bot
  before_action :set_room

  def create
    if create_message
      @message.broadcast_create
      head :created, location: message_path(@message)
    else
      head :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  private
    def authenticate_bot
      @bot = User.authenticate_bot(params[:bot_code])
      head :unauthorized unless @bot
    end

    def set_room
      @room = @bot.rooms.find_by(id: params[:room_id])
      head :not_found unless @room
    end

    def create_message
      if request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"
        create_attachment_message
      else
        create_text_message
      end
    end

    def create_attachment_message
      return unless params[:attachment].respond_to?(:read)

      @message = @room.messages.create_with_attachment!(creator: @bot, attachment: params[:attachment])
    end

    def create_text_message
      body = raw_message_body
      return if body.blank?

      @message = @room.messages.create!(creator: @bot, body: body)
    end

    def raw_message_body
      body = request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding("UTF-8")
      body.valid_encoding? ? body : body.encode("UTF-8", invalid: :replace, undef: :replace)
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class User::BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot generates a bot token and grants membership to open rooms" do
    bot = nil

    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, +Rooms::Open.count do
      bot = User.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    end

    assert bot.bot?
    assert bot.active?
    assert bot.bot_token.present?
    assert_equal Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).sort, bot.rooms.pluck(:id).sort
  end

  test "bot requires a name" do
    bot = User.new(name: "", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

  test "authenticate_bot returns active bot for valid token and nil for invalid or deactivated" do
    bot = User.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    token = bot.bot_token

    assert_equal bot, User.authenticate_bot(token)
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("wrong-token")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot("")
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(nil)

    bot.deactivate
    assert_nil User.authenticate_bot(token)
    assert_nil bot.reload.bot_token
  end

  test "deactivating a bot removes non-direct memberships and preserves messages" do
    bot = User.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    room = rooms(:pets)
    message = room.messages.create!(creator: bot, body: "Deploy finished")

    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, -bot.memberships.without_direct_rooms.count do
      bot.deactivate
    end

    assert bot.reload.deactivated?
    assert Message.exists?(message.id)
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", message.reload.creator.name
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > docs/bots.md
# Chat Bots Design Notes

## Data Model
- Bots are modeled on `User` with `role: :bot` (in `User::Role`: `enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]`) and `User::Bot` concern.
- `users.bot_token` (unique indexed string) stores the bot's secret authentication token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`), generated on creation when `role == "bot"`.
- `users.creator_id` (foreign key to `users`) tracks who created the bot so `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` naturally grants access to administrators and the bot's creator.
- Modeling bots as `User` records allows bots to reuse:
  - `Membership` (auto-joining `Rooms::Open` on creation, toggle-based assignment on `Rooms::Closed`, `@mention` autocomplete, and unread tracking).
  - `Message#creator` (`belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User"`), displaying the bot's name and avatar in messages and web push notifications.
  - `User::Avatar` (`fresh_user_avatar_path`, uploaded avatars, and SVG initials fallback).
- Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate` (sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token` to `nil`, removes non-direct room memberships) so historical messages remain intact with the bot's name while immediately revoking API access.
- Human-only surfaces (`AccountsController`, `Accounts::UsersController`, `SessionsController`, `Sessions::TransfersController`, `Users::BansController`, `Users::SidebarsController`) scope to `User.not_bot` so bots cannot log in, be promoted/banned, or clutter account member lists.

## HTTP API
- `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` handled by `Rooms::BotMessagesController#create`.
- Skips session authentication and CSRF forgery protection; authenticates via `User.authenticate_bot(params[:bot_code])` (`active.bot.find_by(bot_token: ...)`).
- Reads `request.raw_post` (forced to UTF-8) directly as the message body so shell scripts/CI jobs can use `curl -d "..."` without JSON envelopes or form-decoding corruption. Supports `multipart/form-data` with `attachment` file uploads via `create_with_attachment!`.
- Broadcasts the message (`@message.broadcast_create`) and triggers `Room::PushMessageJob` via `Message`'s `after_create_commit` callback.
EOF

    has_many :created_bots, -> { bot }, class_name: "User", foreign_key: :creator_id, dependent: :nullify

      self.bot_token ||= generate_bot_token

      loop do

        break token unless User.exists?(bot_token: token)
      end
    end

require "test_helper"

class Rooms::BotMessagesControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper

  setup do
    host! "once.campfire.test"
    @bot = User.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:kevin))
    @open_room = rooms(:hq)
    @closed_room = rooms(:designers)
  end

  test "posting a raw text message creates message, returns 201 with Location, broadcasts, and pushes notifications" do
    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: [ Room::PushMessageJob ] do
      assert_difference -> { @open_room.messages.count }, 1 do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_token),
          params: "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅",
          headers: {
            "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
            "User-Agent" => "curl/8.5.0"
          }
      end
    end

    message = @open_room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "/messages/#{message.id}", response.headers["Location"]
    assert_equal @bot, message.creator
    assert_equal "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅", message.plain_text_body
  end

  test "raw request body with &, =, and + is preserved without form-decoding mangling" do
    raw = "1 + 1 = 2 & key=val"

    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_token),
      params: raw,
      headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }

    assert_response :created
    assert_equal raw, @open_room.messages.order(:id).last.plain_text_body
  end

  test "posting broadcasts turbo stream showing bot name as author and updates unread rooms" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_token),
      params: "Build green",
      headers: { "Content-Type" => "text/plain" }

    assert_rendered_turbo_stream_broadcast @open_room, :messages, action: "append", target: [ @open_room, :messages ] do
      assert_select ".message__author", text: /Deploy Bot/
      assert_select ".message__body", text: /Build green/
    end

    @open_room.users.each do |member|
      assert_broadcasts UnreadRoomsChannel.stream_name_for(member.id), 1 do
        post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_token),
          params: "Build green #{member.id}",
          headers: { "Content-Type" => "text/plain" }
      end
    end
  end

  test "posting triggers web push notifications for room members" do
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Room::PushMessageJob do
      WebPush.expects(:payload_send).times(Push::Subscription.count)
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_token),
        params: "Release ready",
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "text/plain" }
    end
  end

  test "posting a multipart attachment creates an attachment message" do
    assert_difference -> { @open_room.messages.count }, 1 do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_token),
        params: { attachment: fixture_file_upload("moon.jpg", "image/jpeg") }
    end

    message = @open_room.messages.order(:id).last
    assert_response :created
    assert_equal "/messages/#{message.id}", response.headers["Location"]
    assert message.attachment?
  end

  test "empty body and no attachment returns 422 Unprocessable Content" do
    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_token),
        params: "",
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_token),
        params: "   \n  ",
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "text/plain" }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, @bot.bot_token),
        params: { other: "value" },
        headers: { "Content-Type" => "multipart/form-data" }
    end
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
  end

  test "invalid bot code returns 401 Unauthorized" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, "invalid-code"), params: "Hello"
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "deleted bot can no longer post messages" do
    token = @bot.bot_token
    @bot.deactivate

    assert_no_difference -> { Message.count } do
      post room_bot_messages_url(@open_room, token), params: "Hello"
    end
    assert_response :unauthorized
  end

  test "bad room id returns 404 Not Found" do
    post "/rooms/999999/#{@bot.bot_token}/messages", params: "Hello"
    assert_response :not_found
  end

  test "bot cannot post to closed room until added as a member" do
    post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_token), params: "Hello"
    assert_response :not_found

    @closed_room.memberships.grant_to(@bot)

    post room_bot_messages_url(@closed_room, @bot.bot_token), params: "Now I am in!"
    assert_response :created
  end
end
